scope: Configurable HTTP limits and concurrent atomic persistence

requirements.contract: Concurrent writers own unique 0600 temporary files; readers always see complete JSON; failed replacements leave no temporary files
Collector and reconnect commits cannot roll back durable revisions; readers and state mutations progress while disk commits wait
16 KiB headers and 1 MiB bodies by default; serde/schemars config and server options expose both bounds independently
Exact byte boundaries, including fragmented UTF-8 bodies and split header delimiters, preserve the full payload
Oversize headers/bodies produce 431/413 without invoking the handler; unauthenticated callers cannot force the rest of a body read; ambiguous framing is rejected
Actual post_json calls above 16 KiB, and above 1 MiB when explicitly configured, work through the real HTTP/Unix command conduit

isolation: Ephemeral TCP listeners, per-test Unix sockets, temporary private fixture tokens/cache, in-memory fragmented readers; no production account or daemon
